ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Reproducing episodic and online test-time adaptation under one shared protocol
PROPOSAL: Re-run TPT, C-TPT, TDA, DMN and DPE from their released code on CLIP ViT-B/16 using one checkpoint, one hand-written prompt template and one image preprocessing pipeline, on ImageNet, its 4 shifted variants and 10 fine-grained datasets at resolution 224. Episodic methods get 64 augmented views per image, keeping the 6 most confident, and online methods see the test stream in one fixed random order. Record top-1 accuracy of each method next to the zero-shot model, with 3 stream orders and bootstrap intervals over test images.
CONTROLS: Zero-shot CLIP with the same prompt, a prompt-ensemble baseline needing no adaptation, and a comparison of our numbers with the figures printed in each original paper.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: Gains over zero-shot should be smaller than reported, with some methods inside the bootstrap interval of the ensemble baseline. The plan fails if each method keeps its published advantage over the baseline.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Rebuilding a leaderboard of test-time adaptation methods for CLIP at full scale
PROPOSAL: Re-run TPT, C-TPT, O-TPT, TDA, DMN, DPE, ZERO and WATT from released code on CLIP ViT-B/16 and ViT-B/32 with 3 checkpoint sources and 4 prompt templates, on ImageNet, 4 shifted variants and 10 fine-grained datasets. Episodic methods use 64 and 128 augmented views per image and online methods see 5 stream orders. Record top-1 accuracy per cell and rank methods by mean gain over zero-shot with bootstrap intervals over test images. Report the rank of each method per dataset and the number of datasets where adaptation hurts relative to zero-shot, so that the leaderboard shows spread as well as mean.
CONTROLS: Zero-shot CLIP at each prompt, the prompt-ensemble baseline, and rank agreement between leaderboards from different checkpoints.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: Rankings should shift with the checkpoint source, so that fewer than half of method pairs keep their order. The plan fails if rankings are identical for all 3 checkpoint sources.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Calibration before and after test-time adaptation of CLIP on shifted ImageNet variants
PROPOSAL: Evaluate TPT, C-TPT, TDA and DMN on CLIP ViT-B/16 for expected calibration error, Brier score and confidence histograms on ImageNet-A, ImageNet-R, ImageNet-Sketch, ImageNetV2 and ImageNet itself, with 3 stream orders for the online methods. Fit one temperature on the held-out split of 1000 images and ask whether post-hoc scaling removes the shift in calibration caused by adaptation. Calibration error uses 15 equal-mass bins, and the temperature grid runs from 0.5 to 2.0 in 20 steps. Bootstrap over test images gives intervals for each metric.
CONTROLS: Zero-shot CLIP with and without temperature scaling, a prompt-ensemble baseline, and a randomly relabelled version of the confidence analysis.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: Adaptation should raise accuracy and worsen calibration error on at least 3 of the 5 datasets. The plan fails if the post-hoc temperature restores zero-shot calibration in all of them.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Calibration, selective prediction and confidence drift of test-time adaptation over ten datasets
PROPOSAL: Evaluate TPT, C-TPT, O-TPT, TDA, DMN and ZERO on CLIP ResNet-50 and ViT-B/16 for expected calibration error, Brier score, AURC and confidence histograms on ImageNet, 4 shifted variants and 10 fine-grained sets, with 5 stream orders and 3 temperature fits on held-out splits of 1000 images. Track confidence of a test sample along the stream at positions 100, 500, 1000 and 5000 for online methods, and bootstrap over test images. Summarise each method by the sign of its change in calibration error on each dataset and by how that change relates to its change in accuracy.
CONTROLS: Zero-shot CLIP with temperature scaling, a prompt-ensemble baseline, and a shuffled-stream control for the drift analysis.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: Online methods should drift towards overconfidence late in the stream. The plan fails if confidence at stream position 5000 matches that at position 100 within sampling error.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Does a prompt ensemble match test-time adaptation on fine-grained datasets?
PROPOSAL: Compare zero-shot CLIP ViT-B/16 using an 80-template ensemble against TPT and TDA on 10 fine-grained datasets: Flowers, Pets, Cars, Aircraft, Food, DTD, SUN, EuroSAT, UCF and Caltech. Use one preprocessing pipeline and 3 stream orders for TDA, and give TPT 64 augmented views. Report top-1 accuracy with paired bootstrap intervals over test images and the number of datasets on which each adaptive method beats the ensemble.
CONTROLS: Single-template zero-shot, the ensemble, and an ensemble of the 7 best templates picked on the held-out split of the training images.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: The ensemble should reach most of the gain attributed to adaptation, beating TPT on at least 3 datasets. The plan fails if TPT and TDA beat it on 9 of 10.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A reproducibility audit of reported test-time adaptation gains over checkpoints and prompts
PROPOSAL: Evaluate zero-shot CLIP and TPT, C-TPT, TDA, DMN and ZERO on 10 fine-grained datasets with ViT-B/16 and ResNet-50 image encoders, each taken from 3 checkpoint releases and with the single default template, an 80-template ensemble and 5 handwritten templates per dataset. Report top-1 accuracy per cell and decompose the variance of gain over zero-shot into method, checkpoint, template and dataset terms by analysis of variance, then list the 5 cells where the ranking of methods is most unstable.
CONTROLS: Variance decomposition repeated on label-permuted accuracies, plus a comparison against the figures printed in the original papers.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: Checkpoint and template terms should jointly explain more variance in gain than the method term. The plan fails if the method term alone exceeds 60 percent of the variance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Test-time adaptation applied on top of prompt-tuned CLIP models
PROPOSAL: Train CoOp, MaPLe and PromptSRC on ImageNet with 16 shots per class using CLIP ViT-B/16, then apply TPT, TDA and DMN at test time to each tuned model and to the frozen model, on 4 shifted ImageNet variants and 10 fine-grained datasets. Measure top-1 accuracy and the additive gain of adaptation on each tuned model relative to the gain on the frozen model, with 3 training seeds and 3 stream orders, and bootstrap intervals over test images.
CONTROLS: Tuned model without adaptation, frozen model with adaptation, and a model tuned on 16 shots of the target dataset to separate adaptation from target exposure.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: Gain from adaptation should shrink on tuned models by about half relative to the frozen one. The plan fails if gains are the same size or larger on the tuned models, which would show complement without overlap.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Complement or conflict: test-time adaptation after training-time tuning, with seeds, shots and encoders varied
PROPOSAL: Train CoOp, CoCoOp, MaPLe, PromptSRC and KgCoOp with 1, 4, 8 and 16 shots per class on ImageNet using CLIP ViT-B/16 and ViT-B/32, 3 seeds each, then apply TPT, C-TPT, TDA and DMN to all 120 tuned models on 4 shifted ImageNet variants and 10 fine-grained datasets. Fit a regression of the gain from adaptation on tuning method, shots and baseline accuracy, with bootstrap intervals over test images, and plot the gain of each adapted model against its own starting accuracy.
CONTROLS: Tuned models without adaptation, the frozen model with adaptation, and a regression fitted on randomly permuted gains.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: Gain from adaptation should shrink with the number of shots and with baseline accuracy. The plan fails if the shot coefficient is indistinguishable from zero.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Do test-time adaptation gains carry over to SigLIP and EVA-CLIP?
PROPOSAL: Apply TPT, TDA, DMN and ZERO to SigLIP ViT-B/16, EVA-CLIP ViT-B/16 and OpenCLIP ViT-B/16 trained on LAION-2B, adapting the loss of each method to the sigmoid or softmax output where needed. Evaluate top-1 accuracy on ImageNet, 4 shifted variants and 10 fine-grained datasets with one prompt template and 3 stream orders, and compare the gain over zero-shot with that measured on OpenAI CLIP ViT-B/16 under the same settings.
CONTROLS: Zero-shot for each model with the same prompt, an ensemble baseline, and OpenAI CLIP as the reference for the sign of each gain.
COST: 250
PREDICTION: Gains should shrink for models whose zero-shot accuracy is higher, and turn negative for some methods on SigLIP. The plan fails if each method gains by the same amount on all 4 models.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Test-time adaptation beyond CLIP: sixteen vision-language models and eight methods
PROPOSAL: Apply TPT, C-TPT, TDA, DMN, DPE, ZERO, WATT and CLIPArTT to OpenAI CLIP, OpenCLIP, SigLIP, EVA-CLIP, MetaCLIP, DFN, ALIGN and BLIP, each at 2 sizes, adapting each method's loss to the output form of each model. Evaluate top-1 accuracy on ImageNet, 4 shifted variants and 10 fine-grained datasets with 3 prompt templates and 5 stream orders, and relate gain over zero-shot to model size, pretraining data size and zero-shot accuracy, using 3 size bins and listing each method-model cell whose gain changes sign.
CONTROLS: Zero-shot for each model with the same prompts, an ensemble baseline, and a method-by-model table of the sign of each gain.
COST: 250
PREDICTION: Gain should fall as pretraining data size grows. The plan fails if pretraining data size explains less than 10 percent of the variance of gain across models.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Sensitivity of online adaptation to the order and length of the test stream
PROPOSAL: Run TDA and DMN on CLIP ViT-B/16 over ImageNet and 5 fine-grained datasets, with 20 random stream orders, a class-sorted order and an order with consecutive blocks of one class. Record running top-1 accuracy at positions 100, 500, 1000 and the end, and the standard deviation of final accuracy across orders. Test whether the ranking of the 2 methods flips under any order, with bootstrap intervals over orders.
CONTROLS: Zero-shot accuracy as a flat reference, a memory-free version of each method, and a shuffled-order control for the class-sorted stream.
COST: 36
PREDICTION: Class-sorted and block orders should cut accuracy by a few points relative to random order. The plan fails if standard deviation across random orders exceeds the gap between the two methods.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Order, length and temperature of the stream: online adaptation of CLIP under many stream designs
PROPOSAL: Run TDA, DMN and ZERO-online on CLIP ResNet-50 and ViT-B/16 over ImageNet, 4 shifted variants and 10 fine-grained datasets with 50 random orders, class-sorted orders, block orders of three sizes, and stream lengths of 1000, 5000 and the full test set. Record running top-1 accuracy at 6 positions and the spread of final accuracy across orders, and test whether method rankings flip under any design.
CONTROLS: Zero-shot reference, memory-free versions, and a shuffled-order control for each sorted stream.
COST: 36
PREDICTION: Ranking flips should be common under block orders, with at least 20 percent of dataset-pair cells changing sign. The plan fails if spread across random orders stays under half a point everywhere.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Robustness of test-time adaptation to image corruptions and attacks
PROPOSAL: Evaluate TPT, C-TPT, TDA and DMN on CLIP ViT-B/16 using ImageNet-C at 15 corruption types and severity 3 and 5, plus ImageNet with an L-infinity perturbation of 4/255 generated by 10-step projected gradient descent against the zero-shot model. Record top-1 accuracy and the fraction of corrupted samples whose prediction flips relative to zero-shot, with 3 stream orders for online methods and bootstrap intervals over test images.
CONTROLS: Zero-shot CLIP, a prompt-ensemble baseline, and a transfer-only attack crafted on a different checkpoint to separate gradient masking from robustness.
COST: 700
PREDICTION: Adaptation should give gains on noise corruptions yet help little against the perturbation. The plan fails if gains against the perturbation match gains on clean data.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A robustness study of test-time adaptation over corruptions, severities and attack strengths
PROPOSAL: Evaluate TPT, C-TPT, O-TPT, TDA, DMN, DPE and ZERO on CLIP ViT-B/16 and ViT-B/32 with ImageNet-C at 15 corruption types and 5 severities, and with L-infinity perturbation strengths from 1 to 8 out of 255 generated by projected gradient descent at three step counts against the zero-shot model. Record top-1 accuracy and the fraction of prediction flips relative to zero-shot, with 3 stream orders for online methods and bootstrap intervals.
CONTROLS: Zero-shot CLIP, a prompt-ensemble baseline, and transfer attacks crafted on a different checkpoint.
COST: 700
PREDICTION: Gains should decrease monotonically with perturbation strength. The plan fails if gains at 8 out of 255 are the same as at 1 out of 255.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Out-of-distribution detection with CLIP before and after test-time adaptation
PROPOSAL: Use ImageNet as in-distribution and iNaturalist, SUN, Places and Textures as out-of-distribution sets with CLIP ViT-B/16, scoring by maximum concept matching and by max softmax. Run TPT and TDA to adapt on a mixed stream with 10 percent out-of-distribution images, and report AUROC and false-positive rate at 95 percent recall of in-distribution images, with 3 stream orders and 200 bootstrap resamples over test images, using 1000 images per out-of-distribution set, and add a plot of the score distributions before and after adaptation.
CONTROLS: Zero-shot detection with the same scores, a stream without out-of-distribution images, and a randomly relabelled version of the detection scores.
COST: 90
PREDICTION: Adapting on a mixed stream should lower AUROC by a few points since out-of-distribution samples are pulled into known classes. The plan fails if AUROC is unchanged within the bootstrap interval.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Out-of-distribution detection under test-time adaptation, over contamination levels and scores
PROPOSAL: Use ImageNet as in-distribution and iNaturalist, SUN, Places, Textures, OpenImage-O and NINCO as out-of-distribution sets with CLIP ResNet-50 and ViT-B/16, scoring by maximum concept matching, max softmax, energy and Mahalanobis distance in feature space. Run TPT, C-TPT, TDA and DMN on mixed streams with five contamination levels from 0 to 50 percent, show the score distributions before and after adaptation, and report AUROC and false-positive rate at 95 percent recall, with 3 stream orders and bootstrap intervals.
CONTROLS: Zero-shot detection with the same scores, contamination-free streams, and shuffled detection scores.
COST: 90
PREDICTION: AUROC should decline roughly linearly with contamination for memory-based methods. The plan fails if the 50 percent level shows the same AUROC as the 0 percent level.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: How much does the choice of prompt template change reported adaptation gains?
PROPOSAL: Take TPT and TDA on CLIP ViT-B/16 and evaluate them on ImageNet and 6 fine-grained datasets while changing the starting text prompt among 5 handwritten templates and the 80-template ensemble. Report top-1 accuracy of the adapted model and of zero-shot for each template, the gain, and the Spearman correlation between zero-shot accuracy and gain across templates, with 3 stream orders for TDA and 200 bootstrap resamples over test images.
CONTROLS: Zero-shot for each template, a randomly worded template of the same length, and a correlation computed on shuffled template labels.
COST: 24
PREDICTION: Gain should be negatively correlated with starting accuracy, around minus 0.5, so weak prompts show the largest apparent progress. The plan fails if gain is flat across templates.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Prompt template, checkpoint and preprocessing choices as sources of apparent adaptation progress
PROPOSAL: Take TPT, C-TPT, TDA, DMN and ZERO on CLIP ResNet-50 and ViT-B/16 and evaluate them on ImageNet, 4 shifted variants and 10 fine-grained datasets while changing the starting prompt among 10 handwritten templates and the 80-template ensemble, the checkpoint among 3 releases and the resize interpolation mode. Fit an analysis of variance of gain over zero-shot with these factors, with 3 stream orders and bootstrap intervals over test images.
CONTROLS: Zero-shot for each cell, a randomly worded template of the same length, and variance terms refitted on shuffled gains.
COST: 24
PREDICTION: Starting prompt and checkpoint should account for more of the variance than the method. The plan fails if the method term exceeds all of the other terms combined.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Measuring real progress between early and recent episodic and online methods
PROPOSAL: Order TPT, DiffTPT, C-TPT, RLCF, TDA, DMN, DPE and BoostAdapter by publication date and test whether accuracy rises with date once all are run on CLIP ViT-B/16 under one shared protocol with 2 prompt templates, on ImageNet, 4 shifted variants and 10 fine-grained datasets. Fit a regression of mean gain over zero-shot on date, adding method family as a covariate, with 3 stream orders for online methods and bootstrap intervals over 15 datasets, then plot the fitted trend of each family.
CONTROLS: Zero-shot CLIP, a prompt ensemble, and a regression fitted on randomly permuted dates.
COST: 500
PREDICTION: Gains should grow only slightly with date, with most of the rise coming from the online family. The plan fails if the date coefficient is statistically zero in both families.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Progress curves of test-time adaptation: eight methods compared on three model sizes and two metrics
PROPOSAL: Run TPT, DiffTPT, C-TPT, RLCF, TDA, DMN, DPE and BoostAdapter on CLIP ViT-B/16, ViT-B/32 and ResNet-50 on ImageNet, 4 shifted variants and 10 fine-grained datasets with 2 prompt templates and 5 stream orders, recording top-1 accuracy and expected calibration error. Fit regressions of mean gain over zero-shot on publication date, per family and per model size, with bootstrap intervals over datasets.
CONTROLS: Zero-shot CLIP at each model size, a prompt ensemble, and regressions repeated with permuted dates.
COST: 500
PREDICTION: Date should predict accuracy gain weakly and calibration gain not at all. The plan fails if date explains over 50 percent of variance in both metrics.
